criteria.semantics: A native <button type="submit"> whose text is the button's label: it does something (submits its form), it never goes somewhere (that is a link).

keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to the button and is strongly visually indicated.
Activates the button: its form submits.
Activates the button: its form submits.

criteria.name: The button's label, the same words as its visible text; its purpose is clear from them.
criteria.state: Dimmed or unavailable once the shell disables it after a refusal (a 403); otherwise none.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the button's label grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the button reflow into one column, its label whole and no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <button> element.
The button submits its form: type="submit".
WHEN I use the Tab key I SEE focus reach the button: it is in the tab order, not disabled and with no negative tabindex.
WHEN the button has focus I SEE a focus ring of at least 2px in the focus color.
The button's text is its label, so its accessible name matches what I see.
WHEN I Tab to the button with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its purpose is clear and I HEAR it identify its role of button.
WHEN I swipe to the button with a mobile screen reader (TalkBack, VoiceOver) I HEAR its name and its role of button, and a double tap activates it.
WHEN I press Space or Enter on the button I HEAR the outcome: the status region says what happened, or a refusal names the control.
WHEN the shell has disabled the button after a refusal I HEAR it expressed as dimmed or unavailable.

criteria.semantics: One focusable control in the window's tab order: its label in accent-fg on accent, ringed in the focus color while focused. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Button node named by its label, with a Click action that submits its form, and disabled while it submits (AXButton on macOS, the Button control type with the Invoke pattern on Windows, a push button on AT-SPI).

keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to the button, in reading order, and the focus ring shows.
Focus moves back to the control before it, wrapping to the last.
Submits the button's form (macOS, with Full Keyboard Access; Windows; GNOME).
Submits the button's form (Return on macOS).

criteria.name: The button's label, the same words as its visible text.
criteria.role: Button (VoiceOver: button; Narrator: button; Orca: push button).
criteria.state: Busy while its form submits: the label says (Submitting…) and the button takes no key or click; once there is a tree, unavailable (VoiceOver: dimmed; Narrator: unavailable; Orca: grayed) until it is answered.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the button's label grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the button's label drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the button's label at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the button's label and its focus ring drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) with focus following I SEE the magnifier follow the keyboard focus to the button's label.

check.statement: WHEN the window opens or loads a screen I SEE it hold the keyboard focus, so Tab reaches the button without a click.

WHEN I use Tab and Shift+Tab I SEE focus reach the button in reading order, top to bottom, wrapping at either end, on every platform (macOS' Keyboard navigation setting does not change it: the window keeps its own tab order).
WHEN the button has focus I SEE a 2px ring in the focus color drawn outside it, on the window's ground, a pair the palettes hold to 3:1.
WHEN I press Space or Enter on the focused button I SEE its form submit and the label say (Submitting…) until it is answered.
The button's label is drawn in accent-fg on accent, a pair the palettes hold to the text floor.
WHEN I Tab to the button with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its label and I HEAR it identify its role of button.
WHEN I activate the button with the screen reader's own command (VoiceOver's VO+Space, Narrator's Caps Lock+Enter, Orca's activate) I HEAR its form submit, as Space and Enter do.
WHEN its form is submitting I HEAR the button expressed as dimmed or unavailable, and I HEAR the outcome when it is answered.

announce.api: AXButton, its label as the AXTitle (AccessKit Role::Button with its label); AXEnabled false while it submits; AXPress submits.
announce.says: "Send, button"; while it submits, "Send (Submitting…), dimmed, button".

announce.api: ControlType Button, its label as the Name, IsKeyboardFocusable, IsEnabled false while it submits; the Invoke pattern submits.
announce.says: "Send, button"; while it submits, "Send (Submitting…), button, unavailable".

announce.api: ATSPI_ROLE_PUSH_BUTTON (ATSPI_ROLE_BUTTON), its label as the name, STATE_FOCUSABLE, STATE_SENSITIVE and STATE_ENABLED off while it submits; the Action interface's click submits.
announce.says: "Send, push button"; while it submits, "Send (Submitting…), push button, grayed".

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size, the platform's high contrast and a magnifier following focus, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). No CI job runs the window tests that show the SEE checks; they run by hand (ACCESSIBILITY.md).
